While a model weight miss inevitably triggers a pipeline stall, a KV cache miss is resolved through dynamic recomputation on the GPU. This design choice avoids the inefficiency of retrieving isolated missing blocks from the remote tier, which would necessitate either suboptimal chunk-sized transfers or complex retrieval logic. Consequently, recomputing the missing KV segments directly on the GPU is more performance-efficient [...] ### 4.2. ITME I/O Scheduling and Prefetching

The primary role of ITME is to efficiently orchestrate KV cache movement across the multi-tier hierarchy, leveraging specific access patterns and device characteristics. It manages this entire lifecycle, from migrating blocks immediately upon GPU eviction to proactively prefetching them based on upcoming execution demands.

results.title: Decoding the Jargon and Impact on Samsung, SK Hynix
results.content: The problem emerged as AI began processing data equivalent to dozens of books at once. The notepad (KV cache) fills up almost instantly, creating a bottleneck. Previously, the only option was to spend enormous sums simply adding more memory chips. [...] To understand what TurboQuant is and what impact it may have, one must first decode the alien terminology. AI reads human language by breaking it into units called tokens — fragments of words. As a conversation grows longer, the AI temporarily writes down earlier tokens' context in memory such as HBM so it does not lose track. It is like sticking Post-it notes beside a thick book to remember the content. This temporary AI notepad is called the KV cache (Key-Value Cache).
